title: Is anyone making money scalping XAUUSD with an AI bot?
author: SignificantPeak7614
selftext:
I'm a software engineer exploring the idea of building an AI/ML bot to scalp gold (XAUUSD) on the M1 timeframe.

I'm curious whether anyone here has built or used one successfully.

\* Are you training your own models or using existing ones?

\* Is it actually profitable after spreads and slippage?

\* What win rate and risk-to-reward ratio do you achieve?

I'd appreciate honest experiences, including failures. Is this worth pursuing, or is it mostly a waste of time?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I haven't built one, so I can't give you my own numbers. The cost is the main hurdle on a one-minute chart, because gold's spread and slippage can be a large share of a small target, and a strategy that looks fine before costs often turns negative after them. I'd test with the real spread, including how it widens around news, and judge it by profit per trade over a few thousand trades, not by win rate. A forward test on a demo account for a few weeks will show you the gap between the backtest and real fills. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to test a rule with fees and slippage included.

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body:
I can’t offer personal profitability or win-rate numbers. For an M1 gold model, I’d first check whether the target remains meaningful after spread, fees and adverse slippage, including news periods. Freeze a simple baseline before adding ML, log when signals become available, and compare on unseen data; a higher win rate can still hide much worse tail losses.



Disclosure: we’re QATS. If you decide to explore a prop-perpetuals implementation, try our Trading API docs: [https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/](https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/) . It exposes market data, account/risk state, orders and positions for your own adapter. Check the available instruments and account permissions first; it is not an MT5 EA connector. Evaluations and initial funded accounts are simulated, and using an API doesn’t establish an edge.
